summary: Self-improving coding harness using a Recursive Language Model (RLM) design with a persistent Python REPL and recursive sub-agents. Self-improvement via /refine command that edits harness state (prompt notes, skills, sub-agent config) with rollback snapshots. MIT-licensed, arXiv:2608.23552.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the persistent REPL and recursive sub-agents are architecturally interesting, but AgentForge runs CLI subprocesses sequentially and has no REPL continuity. Skill injection gap is already tracked by HID-188. Self-improvement loop too architectural for 1-2 agent runs.

summary: LangGraph v1.2 introduced a split memory model: a checkpointer for per-thread short-term state and a BaseStore for cross-thread long-term memory with namespaces, semantic search, and explicit write semantics.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — interesting pattern, but AgentForge already ships skill distillation with planner injection (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). The only remaining gap (executor not receiving skills) is tracked by HID-188.

summary: Study showing agents cannot reliably predict their own token/money/time spending. Proposes trained Qwen-7B estimators as budget-awareness signals and an early-stop policy. Budget awareness found to be separate from task performance.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly motivates HID-163 (token cost telemetry). Cannot create new issue; HID-163 already tracks this theme.

summary: Inference-time planner using a learned world model with Monte Carlo lookahead to estimate future tool costs and stay within budget. Finds prompt-based cost feedback alone insufficient. Reports that standalone agents often violate hard budget limits.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — interesting architecture for budget-aware planning, but prerequisite (HID-163 cost telemetry) has not shipped. Would become relevant once measurement data exists.

summary: Karpathy coined 'agentic engineering' in February 2026 as successor to vibe coding. AutoResearch is a 630-line ML experiment automation system running 700 autonomous experiments with 11% training speed gains. No new papers; primarily talks and podcasts in 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AutoResearch is focused on ML experiment automation, not on orchestration patterns applicable to AgentForge's state machine model.

summary: RL-based approach training models to reflect on and correct their own code without external feedback at inference time. Reports 94.51% on HumanEval for 8B model. Code and data publicly available.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — requires model fine-tuning. AgentForge uses off-the-shelf CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex) and cannot retrain them. Pattern is interesting but out of scope for orchestrator-level improvements.

summary: MIT-licensed plugin for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex CLI running autonomous discover-build-audit-ship cycles with eval gating and continuous learning. Draws on Reflexion and double-loop learning. Last pushed June 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — eval gating concept aligns with HID-135 (acceptance-test harness from approved plan). The continuous cycle pattern is similar to HID-72 (auto-dispatch loop). No additive capability beyond open issues.

summary: Microsoft placed AutoGen into maintenance mode in October 2025; new features land in the Microsoft Agent Framework, which reached 1.0 GA on April 2, 2026. AutoGen repository remains installable but accepts no new features.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses a bespoke state machine model. No specific pattern from MAF 1.0 maps to a verified gap in AgentForge's current architecture.

summary: Survey covering frameworks, communication protocols (agent-to-agent, model context protocols), and emerging patterns in LLM-based multi-agent orchestration. Literature cutoff March 2026. Examines LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — general survey with no specific adoptable pattern that isn't already tracked in the backlog or shipped in AgentForge.
